statements.text: So there is a real fear and it is a credible fear out there for those of us that think this could be used or weaponized against a nation's citizenry. [...] I want to ask from your perspective, the significant concerns you have regarding the AI of the future. If anybody wants to talk about election fraud, specifically candidates that can be created to look like they are saying something that they are not actually saying and how that could be generated, the ability for a user and I am not talking about Government regulation here but for a user to have a fact check, something that could be encrypted where I could have the ability to determine whether or not that was created or if that is an actual video?
statements.context: House Homeland Security Committee hearing on AI and homeland defense, where Rep. Brecheen questions witnesses about surveillance and deepfake risks.

statements.text: I think a lot of the questions are centered around the border and how AI can help us be able to identify fraud and also protect entities within the United States.
statements.context: House committee hearing on using AI for homeland security and border enforcement, with industry panelists testifying.

statements.text: This integration of AI into cyber attacks should concern every American. The recent cyber attack leveraging Anthropic's AI infrastructure showed that complex attack campaigns can now be conducted with little to no human interaction, at speeds faster than a human could replicate. [...] The proof of concept is there, and even if U.S.-based AI companies can put safeguards against using their models for such attacks, these actors will find other ways to access this technology. [...] we need to make sure that Federal civilian agencies are taking the proactive steps needed to protect their networks against intrusion. [...] we can't afford to have cybersecurity practices moving at such speeds absent Government interdiction.
statements.context: Opening statement by Rep. Josh Brecheen, Chair of the Subcommittee on Oversight, Investigations, and Accountability, at a joint hearing on AI, quantum, and cloud cybersecurity threats.

statements.text: China, our most significant cyber threat actor, continues to search for new tactics to infiltrate critical U.S. systems, and is prioritizing the development of advanced computing technology and AI that supports its economic and strategic goals.
statements.venue: Opening statement, House Homeland Security joint subcommittee hearing on AI, quantum and cloud cybersecurity

statements.text: As technologies like AI continue to advance at rapid speeds, we must be vigilant and strategic in protecting our intellectual property and national security.
statements.venue: Opening statement, House Homeland Security joint subcommittee hearing on AI, quantum and cloud cybersecurity

statements.text: Recently, @RepOgles and I co-chaired a @HomelandGOP hearing on the impacts of AI on cybersecurity. Congress must stand alert to the fact that Communist China is actively working to weaponize AI, and other emerging technologies, to harm America. We must work with the private sector stand up against the CCP and mitigate cyber threats to our homeland.
statements.quoted:
🚨One month ago, Claude AI was hijacked by the Chinese Communists

Tomorrow, I will have Anthropic explain before my Cyber Committee how they caught these hackers, and what we can do to stop them. No Committee in the House wants to touch this AI issue because it will put a large target on members ’ backs. Having this hearing will put my staff, my family, and every committee member at risk from foreign data hackers. We accept the risk. We will be bold. 

Now that I am Cyber Chairman, I am making this my battle. I will fight the culture war, and now I vow to lead the cyber war. Stay tuned.
